version.value: Abridged orchestral version; which passages are omitted is not documented
version.note: The file lasts 4:06 against a typical performance of 7½–9 minutes (Wikipedia), and the disc is a single 12-inch side. DAHR and the Internet Archive do not describe the cut. This dossier does not locate cut bars.

performers.note: DAHR gives Philadelphia Orchestra and Leopold Stokowski. The Internet Archive item credits “Philadelphia Symphony Orchestra”, a variant of the same ensemble’s name. DAHR’s instrumentation list (7 first violins, 5 second violins, 3 violas, 2 cellos, 4 basses, harp, 3 oboes, 3 clarinets, 2 bassoons, 2 trumpets, 3 trombones, 2 tubas, traps) comes from Victor ledgers for 15 March 1921 and is not confirmed for the issued take.

date.value: 18 April 1921 (issued take 4); earlier takes 1–2 on 15 March 1921
date.note: DAHR: takes 1 and 2 on 15 March 1921 and 3 on 18 April were destroyed; take 4 (18 April 1921) is the issued master. A bracketed [1921] is the date given for the issue on Victor 74698. Some listings give the earlier date for the first takes.

place.note: DAHR gives Camden, New Jersey for every take.

label.note: DAHR describes the object as Victor 74698, Red Seal 12-inch single-faced. Later issues on Victor 6366 and Gramophone Company DB-599 and 3-0662 are listed for the same matrix and take.

catalogue.note: The Internet Archive item also shows matrix and catalogue number 74698 and publisher “Victrola”.

matrixTakeSides.note: The Internet Archive item shows 74698 as its matrix number; the Victor matrix is C-24988.

credits.note: The item metadata names George Blood, L.P. as scanning centre and credits Robert Boggs with metadata and transfer entry and Kevin Coupe with cleaning (as Internet Archive user fields).

date.note: The item’s public date is 19 March 2021; that is the upload date, not a transfer date.

processing.value: Digitised at 78 rpm with four styli (3.8, 2.3, 2.8 and 3.3 mil truncated conical); the preferred version was selected by an engineer at George Blood and copied to the friendly file name
processing.note: The item’s notes say the record was acoustic and that the other side was “not completed due to physical condition of disc”. The MP3 used here is the Internet Archive derivative of the 24-bit FLAC; no further processing is disclosed.

digital.format: VBR MP3 derivative of a 24-bit FLAC transfer

composition.value: Sibelius died in 1957; in countries with a life-plus-70 term the composition remains in copyright until the end of 2027
composition.note: Computed from the composer’s life dates, given in DAHR’s MARC record as 1865–1957. The composition’s status in other territories is not assessed. The programme’s rule applies to the sound recording.

recording.value: Rule 2 — United States public domain: first published in 1921, before the 1926 cut-off.
recording.note: DAHR records the issue on Victor 74698 as [1921]; the brackets mean the year was supplied by the cataloguer, and no month of issue is recorded. The take issued was made on 18 April 1921, so publication followed that date. The Internet Archive item date is also 1921. The item has no licence URL and no non-commercial restriction in its metadata.
